nodes.t: Since March 2023 I’ve been making 10,000 pots, numbered in order. Each pot’s number is its price in pennies: #1 cost a cent, and #10,000 will cost $100. Everything else in this diagram is how the pots get photographed, sold and found.
What has come out of the studio so far.
Made in order through #2,594. 1,741 have sold, $16,330 in all. 853 are made and still for sale.
People can pay for a number before its pot is made. 41 numbers past #2,594 are already spoken for.
Every pot gets a photo so it can be listed. 874 have one so far. 240 of the pots for sale still need one, and I’m shooting the newest first.
A run of pots made in black clay.
A run of slabs in black sculpture clay. They have their own collection on Are.na.
Where a pot can be bought or looked up.
The live shop, where every pot has its own listing. There’s also an email signup for notes from the studio.
Every photographed pot listed by number, with the ranges and techniques behind them. Each one links to its listing in the shop.
A new store that shows all 10,000 numbers on one grid. Tap a hundred to zoom in, find your number, then buy it or reserve it. Not open yet.

nodes.s: made with a tool I built
nodes.t: Sep 30 · A short video of the Haiku Black Slabs, made with reel-machine, a tool I built for making short videos.
How a photo gets from my phone onto a pot’s listing, step by step.
I photograph each pot in a run, one after another. The phone backs every photo up by itself.
Every photo from a session lands in Google Photos, in the order it was taken.
Select the whole run in Google Photos, download it and unzip it into one folder per batch, keeping the original files.
A small tool I built. I load the folder, click the last photo of each pot and type its number.
Each number is checked against exactly one listing, tried once without changing anything, then uploaded. Photos are added, never replacing what’s there.
The new store reads the same photos straight from the shop, so both show the same pots.
